positions.sentence: Instructors must include a statement or policy on generative AI use in every course syllabus.
Instructors should include an AI statement or policy in their course syllabus.
Instructors must clearly tell students what AI use is allowed and not allowed in their course.
Instructors should clearly communicate to students their expectations on whether and how AI may be used.
Instructors must state AI expectations in assignment instructions, marking where AI use is permitted or required.
Instructors should state AI expectations in assignment instructions or descriptions, not only in the syllabus.
Instructors should remind students of the AI policy repeatedly, for each assignment and throughout the semester.
Instructors should communicate AI policies early, at course start, and often, both in writing and orally.
Instructors should be specific in their AI policy, naming permitted and prohibited uses, tools, examples, rationale, and citation or disclosure rules.
Instructors may choose their own approach to AI, may add optional policy statements, and may repeat policies elsewhere.
Instructors should not leave AI expectations ambiguous or assume students already know the rules.
Programs, units and administrators should set and communicate AI expectations and syllabus requirements for faculty and students.
Policies state that clear AI statements help students understand expectations and that missing guidance causes confusion.
Policies note that unclear or absent AI statements make it hard to address academic misconduct.
